newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Low-octane bearish on India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Low-octane bearish on India.

text.p: Gasoline firmed with the 95-octane grade traded at $23.80 per barrel but 92-octane was offered unsuccessfully as low-octane was bearish amid the cancellation of Indian's import tender, traders said on Monday.
Unleaded 95-octane lifting August 12-16 was sold by a Dutch trader at $23.80 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore to a Japanese refiner, traders said.
A European major, bidding up the 97-octane last week, reemerged as a seller of 92-octane, offering down intraday to $22.80 from $23.00, the major said.
The major said it stopped bidding the 97-octane as its requirement was for first-half August but it did not have any outstanding shortcovering demand.

The major has sold August delivery 97-octane cargoes to the Philippines refiner Petron Corp and Malaysia at around 60-80 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, sources said.

Sentiment on the low-octane market was bearish amid news that state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has cancelled its tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of 87.15 octane leaded gasoline for delivery to Kandla on the west coast August 10-14.
Traders said there was no reason given for the cancellation of the tender which closed on July 24 and was valid for one day.
They also said no further details were given whether or not IOC planned to reissue the tender.
IOC last issued a tender in June due to a gasoline shortfall caused by the five-day emergency shutdown in early June of the 150,000-barrel-per-day Cochin refinery.

It bought one 25,000-tonne gasoline cargo for June 18-22 delivery at $43 per tonne over MidEast naphtha quotes and another at more than $30 per tonne premium for June 26-30 delivery, both on a c+f basis to Bombay on the west coast,
traders said.
Naphtha remained in backwardation of around five cents per barrel with August quoted at $21.80/$21.95 and September at $21.70/$21.90, up over 30 cents from Friday.
But on the physical market, demand remained muted with traders assessing the fob Singapore premium at around 30-40 cents per barrel.
The only outstanding purchase tender is from Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) CHIP.CN for 28,000 tonnes of N+A for September 11-20 delivery, a company offcial said on Monday.
The tender, which seeks the cargo on a c+f basis to Kaohsiung, closes on July 31 and is valid for one day.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded a tender to sell 27,000-tonnes of Madras low aromatic naphtha lifting August 6-8 to South Korea's Hanwha Chemical Corp at around $19 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob, higher than its last award at a $21 discount for July 6-8 cargo.
IOC also sold by tender a 27,000 tonnes of August 3-5 lifting Bombay HAN to Dutch trader Vitol at around $28 per tonne below U.S. Gulf Coast 87-octane gasoline quotes, fob.
In its last Bombay HAN tender, IOC sold a July 2-4 lifting cargo at around $30 per tonne discount to Japanese spot quotes, fob.
